text: Back-of-the-envelope estimation — turning last lesson's requirements into actual, usable numbers.

Two hundred thousand trips a day, at roughly 500 bytes each, comes out to about 2 to 3 events per second on average, and around 36 and a half gigabytes a year. Deliberately rough — round numbers, simple math.

That scale fits comfortably in a single KQL database, no sharding needed. A hundred times that scale is a genuinely different problem, where partitioning and capacity planning actually start to matter.
The order of magnitude, done fast, beats a precise number done never. Next up: choosing storage — OLTP versus OLAP versus object storage, now that the scale is known.
